message.reasoning: The user asks "is vs code running". They want to know if VS Code is running. We can check if the process is running. But we don't have direct OS access. We can use the cmd_controller_execute tool to run a command that checks if VS Code is running. On Windows, we can use tasklist or powershell. For example: tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe" | findstr /I "Code.exe". If found, it's running. Or use PowerShell: Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue. But we need to return something. We can run a command that outputs whether it's running. Let's do: powershell -Command "Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Id". That will output the process ID if running. Then we can interpret. But we can't parse output. We can just run a command that prints "Running" or "Not running". Use powershell: if (Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Write-Output "Running" } else { Write-Output "Not running" }. So command: powershell -Command "if (Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Write-Output 'Running' } else { Write-Output 'Not running' }". We'll execute that.
